events.title: Edward the Confessor dies, leaving England's throne disputed
events.description: King Edward died at Westminster without children. Rival claims by Harold Godwinson, Harald Hardrada and William of Normandy led to two invasions and the Norman Conquest that autumn.
events.html: King Edward died at Westminster without children. Rival claims by Harold Godwinson, Harald Hardrada and William of Normandy led to two invasions and the Norman Conquest that autumn.

events.title: Charles the Bold of Burgundy killed at the Battle of Nancy
events.description: Duke Charles the Bold died fighting Swiss and Lorrainer troops outside Nancy. His death ended Burgundian ambitions to become a kingdom, and his lands were divided between France and the Habsburgs.

events.title: Turenne defeats the imperial and Brandenburg armies at Turckheim
events.description: During the Franco-Dutch War, the French army under Marshal Turenne made a surprise winter march through the Vosges and defeated the imperial and Brandenburg forces near Colmar. The victory drove the Germans back across the Rhine and secured Alsace for Louis XIV.

events.title: Robert-François Damiens attempts to assassinate Louis XV
events.description: At Versailles, Damiens stabbed Louis XV with a penknife, causing only a slight wound. He was later executed with notorious cruelty, the last person in France to be put to death by quartering.

events.title: Alfred Dreyfus is publicly stripped of his rank in Paris
events.description: Captain Alfred Dreyfus, wrongly convicted of treason in December 1894, was degraded at the Military School in Paris: his badges were torn off and his sword broken. Still protesting his innocence, he was sent to Devil's Island.

events.title: German Workers' Party founded in Munich
events.description: Railway locksmith Anton Drexler founded the small nationalist German Workers' Party. Adolf Hitler joined that autumn and in 1920 the party was renamed the National Socialist German Workers' Party.

events.title: Construction of the Golden Gate Bridge begins
events.description: Work began on a bridge across the Golden Gate strait at the entrance to San Francisco Bay. Opened in 1937, its 1,280-metre main span was the longest in the world until 1964.

events.title: Alexander Dubček takes charge in Czechoslovakia
events.description: Dubček replaced Antonín Novotný as leader of the Czechoslovak Communist Party. His reforms, 'socialism with a human face', inspired the Prague Spring, ended by a Warsaw Pact invasion in August.
